title: Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) - Digital Database and Corresponding Interfaces for ReUse of Architectural Components (v0.6.1.1)
description:
The Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) is a prototypical digital component database. It catalogs digital representations of uniquely identifiable architectural components for reuse. Furthermore, it provides corresponding interfaces and tools to leverage them via a backend REST-API, a web-frontend as well as a interface for direct interaction within Rhino Grasshopper.

Changes in v0.6.1.1 (unreleased)

A security patch (decision 8.144), from a read-only review of 0.6.1.0 in five areas: backend authentication, injection and uploads, authorisation, infrastructure and CI, and the frontend. The review found nothing critical or high; this release takes the small fixes. The larger structural items (one load-and-authorise helper, a shared rate-limit store, a Content-Security-Policy with nonces, signed checksums, PyJWT, the module splits) go to 0.6.2. No change to the Grasshopper components and no migration of records.

Security

  • One sign-in verifier: the web sign-in sends the credentials to POST /auth/token and nowhere else, so the backend's rate limit sees every attempt. The frontend has no database access any more (mongodb, bcryptjs, lib/mongodb.ts and the MONGODB_* variables are gone), and its log line holds the outcome only, never what was typed.
  • Headers: the web app sends frame-ancestors 'none' with X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and, on the canonical host only, HSTS (no includeSubDomains).
  • Server-side calls from the Browse, component and /id pages go to FASTAPI_URL with the session's token, not to a base built from the request's Host header.
  • Invitations: in a dataset an admin has not reviewed yet, a moderator invites only. POST /invitations and POST /datasets/{did}/members answer invited for every address and send the same mail, so neither route tells whether an address has an account. An existing account joins by opening the link in the mail signed in with that address and accepting (/invite, POST /invitations/accept); a new address registers with the code as before. Admins and moderators of a reviewed dataset keep the direct add. At most 50 invitation mails per user per day (new, resent and member-by-email; admins exempt), counted in the database, answered with 429. Member e-mail addresses are shown to admins and to moderators of a reviewed dataset only. Resend needs the caller's current invite permission, not the creation of the invitation.
  • Logs hold no people: no user names, e-mail addresses or typed identifiers in the cron jobs, the web sign-in or the member notices; mail errors are logged by kind. Every site log keeps 14 days, so the privacy page holds as written.
  • Error answers carry no file path, stored document or driver message: a 500 has one text, /health/db answers {"ok": false} with 503, and the cause goes to the log. Validation messages meant for the client (422) stay.
  • Sign-in details: a sign-in with an unknown identifier takes the same password check as a real one; the verification token is stored as a SHA-256 hash (a link mailed before the deploy works until it expires, at most 24 hours); the resend route takes a typed body, always gives the same answer, sends in the background and sends at most three mails an hour per address; a second registration for the same address meets the unique index and answers 409; a JWT_SECRET under 32 bytes stops the backend from starting; a token is looked up by its subject only.
  • Uploads: photos are sniffed by their first bytes and decoded as JPEG, PNG or WebP only, with a 40 megapixel cap checked before any pixel is decoded (also for evidence images); meshes are loaded without their materials; the catalogue filters original_function, material and dataset match their text exactly and have a length cap.
  • Blocking work off the event loop: OBJ conversion, mesh exports and photo decoding run in worker threads; the mesh downloads are rate limited (120 a minute per user or address) and OBJ conversion is refused for files above 50 MB.
  • Proxies: gunicorn trusts the same proxies as the rate limiter (CSC_TRUSTED_PROXIES); the PDF and CERO ETags hold the bases of their links, so a request for another host is never served a document cached for this one.
  • Anonymous dataset list shows a dataset by the same rule as its count: published, not withdrawn, public.
  • CI: every action is pinned to a commit (Dependabot proposes updates weekly); the release workflow writes to the repository in its publish job only.

Changed

  • The invitation mail links to /invite?code=... for every recipient; a new page shows what the invitation offers and takes the acceptance.
  • The privacy page says that the sign-in cookie lasts at most 24 hours, that accounts are deleted on request and that location data is removed from photos.
  • The cron jobs write one dated log a day (<job>_cronjob.<date>.log) and one daily line deletes the cron and deploy logs older than 14 days; the geometry runner and the component map share a lock in ~/csc/shared/locks/heavy.lock instead of /tmp. The deploy gate writes deploy.<date>.log.
  • usermaintenance.py also removes accounts whose verification expiry is stored as text, and uses the configured database name.
  • Pinned in constraints.txt: fastapi, starlette, uvicorn, gunicorn and reportlab, to the versions the backend is tested with; trimesh>=5.

Server notes

  • Check the production JWT_SECRET first: it must be at least 32 bytes (openssl rand -hex 32 gives 64). The backend refuses to start with a shorter one. Locally, put a longer JWT_SECRET into src/backend/dev.env (the example has one).
  • mkdir -p ~/csc/shared/locks, then paste the new crontab.example; after its first runs delete the old undated ~/csc/shared/logs/*_cronjob.log files.
  • The frontend .env loses MONGODB_URI, MONGODB_DB and MONGODB_USERCOLLECTION (harmless if left).
  • If CSC_TRUSTED_PROXIES is set, gunicorn now reads it too: check that every entry is an address or a network (a typo stops the start with its name).
  • The deploy builds a new venv (trimesh>=5, new pins).
  • In the GitHub settings: let the production environment require a reviewer and protect the tags v*.
  • Nobody is signed out by this release, unless JWT_SECRET is changed.

Full history: CHANGELOG.md
